findings.title: Early-dispatch probe still uses the old `createdBy: "user"` command shape
findings.body: The `recovery:early` dispatch hand-builds the same `message.dispatch` that `limitRecoveryCommand` now emits with `createdBy: "agent"`. It still says `createdBy: "user"`. The assertion that it is rejected holds either way, because the usage-limit guard at `Orchestrator.ts:5524-5565` does not read `createdBy`. But the probe no longer matches what the worker sends. It also still goes through the `createdBy === "user"` branch of `mayStartSubagentFollowup`, not the new `usageLimitContinuationOfRunId` branch. Use `createdBy: "agent"` so the probe matches the real command.

contracts.action: Usage-limit auto-resume `message.dispatch` is now attributed to `createdBy: "agent"` (creationSource "server") instead of "user".
contracts.equivalent_path: Other server-originated continuations already use createdBy "agent", for example RestartContinuation.ts:326, IdleCompactionService.ts:117 and ProviderContinuationService.ts:128.
contracts.before_after: Before, the resume message counted as a user-authored message. Now it does not, so these readers treat it as unattended agent input: ProjectionStore.ts:1572 (`latestUserAuthoredMessageAt`), threadHistoryPaging.ts:300 (`isThreadHistoryUserTurn`), ProviderUsageAnalytics.ts:212 (`requestKind` now reports "agent", not "user") and Orchestrator.ts:2465 (`releaseUnattendedHolds`, whose unattended set is built from the held queued messages, not the completed run's message). `sentByUserFromClient` at Orchestrator.ts:5994 was already false because creationSource is "server", so held-queue release at dispatch is unchanged.
contracts.visible_effect: Analytics label the resume as agent-originated. History paging no longer counts the resume as a user turn. A stale waiting-on-user item is no longer cleared by an auto-resume. All of these match the intent of 'attribute to T3 Code'.

contracts.action: Resume commands that carry `usageLimitContinuationOfRunId` are treated as subagent follow-ups, in the lock selection, in `recordSubagentFollowup` and in the sender check.
contracts.equivalent_path: User and MCP follow-ups to an app-owned subagent child: `mayStartSubagentFollowup` selects the parent lock at Orchestrator.ts:13819-13830, and `recordSubagentFollowup` binds a new delegated task to the child's new run at Orchestrator.ts:8020-8105.
contracts.before_after: Before, a resume command with createdBy "user" passed `mayStartSubagentFollowup` and the sender check, so the child's resumed run was tracked as a follow-up. Switching to "agent" would have dropped it silently. The two added `usageLimitContinuationOfRunId` clauses (lines 707 and 8048) keep that behaviour. The dispatch lock is unchanged: parent first, then child. The new task's `createdBy` becomes "agent" (line 8086), the same as MCP follow-ups.
contracts.visible_effect: A child that hit its usage limit and was auto-resumed still gets a pending delegated task on the parent, so the parent is woken when the child finishes.
contracts.failure_mode: If the clause were missing, the resumed child run would have no delegated task, and the parent would never be woken for the result. Covered by the new test.

summary: The change looks correct. Switching the auto-resume to `createdBy: \"agent\"` would have silently dropped the child's resumed run from subagent follow-up tracking. The two added `usageLimitContinuationOfRunId` clauses in `Orchestrator.ts` (lines 707 and 8048) preserve it. I read the other readers of `createdBy === \"user\"` that the new attribution changes: `ProjectionStore.ts:1572`, `threadHistoryPaging.ts:300`, the analytics `requestKind`, and `releaseUnattendedHolds`. Each effect is consistent with attributing the resume to T3 Code. The new delegated-completion test and the `runtimeLayer.test.ts` assertion cover the changed behaviour. I did not run any tests. One small test inconsistency remains: the `recovery:early` probe in `runtimeLayer.test.ts` still builds its command with `createdBy: \"user\"`.
